newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank to stabilise interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank to stabilise interbank rate.

text.p: Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday the central bank will try to maintain the stability of short-term interest rates to ensure that long-term interest rates continue to drop.

"The overnight interbank rate for the rest of this year should not be higher than 11 percent. If it goes higher than that level, the central bank will make some intervention," Rerngchai told reporters.

The interbank was trading around 7.00-7.50 percent on Monday. The rate has fallen sharply after the past few weeks following a recent call by Rerngchai for banks to lower interest rates to boost the economy.
The interbank rate rose as high as 13.00-13.50 percent in the middle of November.
The Bank of Thailand is also developing several new monetary operations in order to reduce the volatility of money and short-term interest rates, Rerngchai said.
He said local interest rates will continue to ease further, but at a gradual pace due to commercial banks' concern about the impact on their profits.
"The local interest rates will gradually decline. If banks sharply cut their interest rates, it will have some impact on their earnings," the governor said.
Most major banks have cut lending and deposit rates by at least 25 basis points following Rerngchai's recent comments.
Rerngchai said the Bank of Thailand on Sunday had briefed the new finance minister, Amnuay Viravan, about the nation's economic picture.
"Many economic figures indicate that the economy is in the depression period. But there were also some signs of recovery," Rerngchai said.
Rerngchai said the current account deficit next year should improve as exports are likely to rise.
The Bank of Thailand said last week the current account deficit this year will be around the same level as in 1995 when it amounted to 8.1 percent of gross domestic product.
